solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Destroy Scottish island (no small island)

indicators.note: 'no' says the following item is to be left out of the island's name

blocks.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An order to wipe out a Hebridean island, with a pedantic bracket about not counting a little islet.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I from the front of ISLAY to leave SLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To slay is to kill, a straightforward synonym for destroy a living thing.

clue.text: Tortures pastors conjured up, having caught highway thief

indicators.note: something conjured up is magicked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
having caught something means holding it inside, so the thief goes within the shuffled letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a pad is an old word for a highwayman, as in footpad

explanation.surface: Clergymen magically produce instruments of torture after catching a highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: The strappado was a torture in which the victim was hoisted by a rope tied to the wrists and dropped.

clue.text: Solitary person outside a public library, say?

indicators.note: 'outside' puts the word for a solitary person around the following letter

blocks.note: a loner keeps to themselves
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recluse standing outside the public library.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'say?' warns the library is only an example of something that lends.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaner is one who lends, and a public library exists to lend books.

clue.text: Summon old expert to squash common fellow

indicators.note: squashing something in presses it inside, so the word for a common fellow goes within the word for expert

blocks.note: an ace is an expert
cit is an old contemptuous word for a townsman or citizen

explanation.surface: A call for a veteran expert to crush an ordinary chap.
explanation.walkthrough: Cit, short for citizen, was an old sneer at a mere townsman, which is why it fits 'common fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Accite is an obsolete verb for calling or citing someone, so to summon in old usage.

clue.text: Harmony around home associated with a fireplace

indicators.note: 'around' puts the word for harmony on both sides of the word for home

blocks.note: to be in chime is to be in harmony
being in is being at home
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note on domestic harmony and the hearth at the centre of the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' looks like part of the domestic picture but is just the word for being at home, which sits inside the harmony word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiminea is a free-standing clay outdoor stove with a chimney, a kind of portable fireplace.

clue.text: Blackmail coming from China not acceptable

blocks.note: CH is an abbreviation for China
out means not acceptable, as in that's out

explanation.surface: An extortion racket based in China being ruled unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Chout was a levy extorted by the Marathas in India, hence blackmail or extortion in Chambers.

clue.text: Islander, one wearing headgear — a Scotsman?

indicators.note: something worn on the head goes around it, so the headgear surrounds the one

blocks.note: a hat is headgear
I is the Roman numeral one
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: Puzzling over whether someone from an island wearing a hat is a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scotsman is not a definition but a typical Scottish first name; the islander is the one being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A Haitian is a native of Haiti, which shares the Caribbean island of Hispaniola.

clue.text: Opinion being heard, proceeded secretly

indicators.note: 'being heard' means we go by how the word for opinion sounds when spoken

blocks.note: to my mind means in my opinion

explanation.surface: Someone voicing a view while quietly getting on with things.
explanation.definitionFit: To mine is to dig tunnels, and figuratively to work underhandedly, as in undermine, so to proceed secretly.

clue.text: Centres in which one sees any number slave, cruelly exploited

indicators.note: something cruelly exploited is knocked about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: n stands for an indefinite number in maths
taken as written

explanation.surface: Places where countless slaves are seen being brutally used.
explanation.definitionFit: The navel is the centre of the belly, and by extension the central point of anything.

clue.text: Friendly agreement? Not with one of two knights opinionated

indicators.note: 'Not with' says the agreement is to be taken without the named item

blocks.note: an entente cordiale is a friendly understanding between nations
N is the chess notation for knight; the word has two

explanation.surface: A friendly deal that one of a pair of knights stubbornly won't join.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one of the two Ns from ENTENTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Entete, from French, means obstinate or headstrong, holding stubbornly to one's views.

clue.text: Bacon that I get cooked for flatmate?

indicators.note: food that gets cooked is transformed, so the letters are made over into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frying breakfast bacon for the person they share a flat with.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a flatmate is only one example of a person living with another.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohabitant is anyone who lives with someone else, of whom a flatmate is one example.

clue.text: Vehicle reversing by French river stopping short — something scraping

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so its word is read right to left
stopping short means falling short of the end, so the river's last letter goes

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
the Loire is France's longest river

explanation.surface: A driver backing up beside a French river and pulling up before reaching it, with a scraping noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A racloir is a prehistoric flint scraper, a tool for scraping hides, hence something scraping.

clue.text: Bishop is coming in ruined, upset, in knots

indicators.note: in a down entry, something upset is turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top
'is coming in' says the churchman enters inside the other word

blocks.note: sunk means done for, ruined
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman arrives ruined and upset, his stomach in knots.
explanation.definitionFit: Knurrs are knots or hard lumps, especially knots in wood, a variant of knur.

clue.text: Embroiderers in Cheshire town registers

blocks.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, England
a register is a list

explanation.surface: Needleworkers recorded in the registers of an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewelists do crewel work, embroidery in loosely twisted worsted yarn.

clue.text: Little old dam like this bursting? Caution!

indicators.note: something bursting breaks apart, so its letters scatter and regroup

blocks.note: a little old, the abbreviation O for old, is the extra letter in the warning word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning shouted as a small old dam threatens to burst.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: the answer plus O for old, burst apart, makes CAUTION. So take O out of CAUTION and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An anicut is an Indian term for a dam or weir built across a river for irrigation.

clue.text: My lord always backing soldiers

indicators.note: 'backing' says the word for always comes behind, supporting the troops from the rear

blocks.note: soldiers as men in the ranks
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A nobleman forever standing behind his troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers come first and 'always' follows them.
explanation.definitionFit: Meneer is the Afrikaans form of address equivalent to sir or Mr, Chambers glossing it as lord.

clue.text: Internet facility providing e-tunes possibly?

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters are only one possible arrangement of what is needed

blocks.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether an online service might supply downloadable music.
explanation.definitionFit: Usenet is the worldwide system of discussion newsgroups, one of the oldest services on the internet.

clue.text: Papal licence in the name of God ultimately

blocks.note: I.N.D. abbreviates the Latin in nomine Dei
ult. abbreviates ultimo or ultimately

explanation.surface: A dispensation granted by the Pope, issued in God's name in the last resort.
explanation.definitionFit: An indult is a special licence or dispensation granted by the Pope from the ordinary rules of canon law.

clue.text: Quiet repose making one ready, as before

blocks.note: p is the musical marking piano, quietly
rest is repose

explanation.surface: A spell of quiet rest that leaves someone refreshed and ready again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' marks the definition as an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Prest is an obsolete adjective for ready or prepared, from Old French, hence 'as before', meaning formerly.

clue.text: No longer chase after prize money, having got weak

blocks.note: a purse is the prize money in a boxing match or race
W is the abbreviation for weak

explanation.surface: A boxer who has gone soft and stopped chasing the prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the definition as an obsolete spelling, not a negative.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursew is an old Spenserian spelling of pursue, meaning to chase after.

clue.text: Tree in China at foot of which is girl

blocks.note: in rhyming slang, china plate means mate, so a pal
Myra is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tree from China with a girl sitting at its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at foot of which' places the girl below the friend in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The palmyra is an Asian palm tree grown for its sap, leaves and timber.

clue.text: Difficult summer month to bear at one time

blocks.note: Aug. abbreviates August
ean is an obsolete verb meaning to give birth, as of ewes

explanation.surface: A summer month that was hard to endure in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at one time' marks EAN as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: An Augean task is filthy and hugely difficult, after Hercules cleaning the stables of King Augeas.

clue.text: Cart heading off to deliver piece of armour

indicators.note: 'heading off' means the head, the first letter, is removed

blocks.note: a tumbrel is a cart, famous for taking victims to the guillotine

explanation.surface: A cart setting off to bring a piece of armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbrel is a variant of umbrere, the movable visor on a helmet that shaded the face.

clue.text: Crocodile gets through biting into girl

indicators.note: something biting into another sinks into it, so the word for through goes inside the word for girl

blocks.note: gal is a casual word for a girl
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: A crocodile gets its teeth through a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Gavial is the older spelling of gharial, from a misreading of the Hindi name.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavial, or gharial, is a long-snouted crocodilian of Indian rivers.

clue.text: Old-fashioned counsel taken on board by daredevil

indicators.note: something taken on board is carried inside, so the answer sits within the next word

blocks.note: the letters run inside this word

explanation.surface: Old-school advice being accepted by a reckless risk-taker.
explanation.definitionFit: Arede is an archaic verb meaning to counsel or advise, a variant of areed.

clue.text: Net for fish gets some quite sleepy going upstream

indicators.note: 'some' of the following words means only a part of them is taken
going upstream in a down entry means running from bottom to top, against the flow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A drowsy fish swimming upriver ends up in a net.
explanation.definitionFit: An eelset is a net set across a river to catch eels, so a net for fish.

clue.text: I'm stupid, restricting power and seeking peace

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the exclamation goes around the word for power

blocks.note: d'oh is Homer Simpson's cry on realising he has been stupid
vis is Latin for force or power

explanation.surface: Someone admits their foolishness in holding power while wanting peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm stupid' is not a confession but the exclamation used to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dovish means favouring negotiation over war, the dove being the bird of peace.

clue.text: Vassal set to provide cattle food

blocks.note: a feudal lord's man was his vassal
to gel is to set, like a jelly

explanation.surface: A feudal vassal assigned to feed the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangel, or mangel-wurzel, is a large beet grown chiefly as fodder for cattle.

clue.text: Like wine that's dull from US but with hidden power

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked inside, so the letter for power goes within the colour

blocks.note: gray is the American spelling of grey, dull
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A flat American wine that nonetheless has hidden strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapy means tasting of or resembling grapes, as wine made from them may.

clue.text: Prohibition slapped on revolutionary army in part of Hungary

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the army's letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a ban is a prohibition
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A ban imposed on a rebel army in a Hungarian district.
explanation.definitionFit: The Banat is a historical region of Hungary, now divided between Romania, Serbia and Hungary.

clue.text: Come face to face with old bishop and one new to the faith

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
B is the chess notation for bishop
a vert is a convert, short for the full word

explanation.surface: A newly converted believer meeting an elderly bishop in person.
explanation.definitionFit: To obvert is to turn something so its front faces you, hence turning towards or confronting.

clue.text: Learned man to mistreat half a dozen

blocks.note: to maul is to handle roughly
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A scholar who manhandles six people.
explanation.definitionFit: A maulvi is a Muslim doctor of the law, a learned teacher in South Asia.

clue.text: Afterwards girl comes to meaningful agreement

blocks.note: syne is Scots for afterwards, as in auld lang syne
sis is short for sister, a girl

explanation.surface: A girl who later comes round to a meaningful agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Synesis is grammatical agreement by sense rather than form, as in 'the crowd were', agreement governed by meaning.

clue.text: Dearies apt to get excited get breathless

indicators.note: being excited means being stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Sweethearts prone to excitement end up gasping for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathless' here is the phonetic sense: losing the breath of an aspirated sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To deaspirate is to pronounce a sound without its aspiration, removing the breathy h, so losing breath.

clue.text: Homeless creature? Everyone needs to have food, Young Conservative admitted

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so the two-letter party abbreviation goes within the word for having food

blocks.note: everyone is all
to eat is to have food
YC abbreviates Young Conservative

explanation.surface: A plea that everyone, the homeless included, needs feeding, with a young Tory let in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Young Conservatives were the youth wing of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley cat is a stray cat living on the streets, so a homeless animal; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: Letters from fourth man circulating

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the first letter of the name moves round to the end

blocks.note: in Genesis, after Adam, Cain and Abel, Seth is the fourth man named

explanation.surface: Correspondence coming from some fourth man who is going around.
explanation.walkthrough: The S moves from front to back of SETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Eth is the Old English letter for the th sound, so eths are letters of the alphabet, not mail.
